questions.question: If 30 January 2010 was Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 01 March 2011?
questions.solution:
There was no leap year in 2010 and 2011 so the on 30th January 2011 there will be a shift by only one day.

That is on 30th January 2011 it will be Sunday.

Total number of days from 30th January 2011 to 01 March 2011:

1 + 28 + 1 = 30 days = 2 odd days 

So, **Sunday + 2 = Tuesday**

Hence **the correct answer is option 2)**

questions.question:
Two different positions of the same dice are shown, the six faces of which are numbered from 1 to 6. Select the number that will be on the face opposite to the one showing '6'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50c1e343ea524d7b799288e60b29a0f3fcadf7462e05e272b56b01029bebc312.png]
questions.solution:
Here, can see that we are given two dices each having one face same i.e. 6. 

We will write the numbers in clockwise direction starting from the common face, then the positional number will be the opposite face of that number.

So,

1st dice: 6 - 5 - 4

2nd dice: 6 - 2 - 3

Also, we can see both the dices have number 6 on the same side and the remaining numbers are shown on both the dices except number 1.

Hence, number __**1**__ will be on the face opposite to the one showing number 6.

Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation.

41 * 3 * 53 * 48 * 3 * 18 * 5 * 36
questions.solution:
Here, we will substitute each option to check which is the correct answer.

First, 

41 times 3 times 53 times 48 times 3 times 18 times 5 times 36

Substitute option 1, we will get,

Rightarrow 41 - 3 times 53 - 48 = 3 + 18 times 5 - 36

Using BODMAS rule, we will get,

Rightarrow 41 - 3 times 53 - 48 = 3 + 18 times 5 - 36

Rightarrow 41 - 159 - 48 = 3 + 90 - 36

Rightarrow -166 = -107

​Rightarrow 166 = 107, which is not possible and so, option 1 is not possible.​

 

Next, 

41 times 3 times 53 times 48 times 3 times 18 times 5 times 36

Substitute option 2, we will get,

Rightarrow 41 - 3 = 53 + 48 times 3 - 18 div 5 + 36

Using BODMAS rule, we will get,

Rightarrow 38 = 53 + 144 - 3.6 + 36

Rightarrow 38 = 229.4, which is not possible and so, option 2 is not possible.​

 

Again, 

41 times 3 times 53 times 48 times 3 times 18 times 5 times 36

Substitute option 3, we will get,

Rightarrow 41 times 3 - 53 = 48 div 3 + 18 times 5 - 36

Using BODMAS rule, we will get,

Rightarrow 123 - 53 = 16 + 90 - 36 

Rightarrow 70 = 70, which is possible and so, option 3 is the correct option.​

 

Last, 

41 times 3 times 53 times 48 times 3 times 18 times 5 times 36

Substitute option 4, we will get,

Rightarrow 41 + 3 - 53 times 48 + 3 = 18 times 5 ​​div 36​

Using BODMAS rule, we will get,

Rightarrow 41 + 3 - 2544 + 3 = 18 ​​times 0.1388

Rightarrow- 2497 = 2.5, which is not possible and so, option 4 is not possible.​

Hence, the correct option is **3.**

questions.question:
If ‘A’ denotes ‘+’, ‘B’ denotes ‘×’, ‘C’ denotes ‘–’ and ‘D’ denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation?

(48 D 12) C 71 A 14 B (96 D 6) A 3 B 12 = ?
questions.solution:
Here, we are given with an equation as below:

(48 D 12) C 71 A 14 B (96 D 6) A 3 B 12 = ?

Next, we will substitute the signs in place of letters given as ‘A’ denotes ‘+’, ‘B’ denotes ‘×’, ‘C’ denotes ‘–’ and ‘D’ denotes ‘÷, we will get,

 = (48 div 12) - 71 + 14 times (96 div 6) + 3 times 12 

Using BODMAS rule, we will get,

= (4) - 71 + 14 times (16) + 36

Opening the brackets, we will get,

= 4 - 71 + 14 times 16 + 36

= - 67 + 224 + 36

= 193

Hence, the correct answer is __**193**__.

questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All plants are herbs.

Some herbs are trees.

All trees are shrubs.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some shrubs are plants.

II. Some shrubs are herbs.

III. Some trees are plants.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Here, we are given some statements and from that we need to find out if the given conclusions are true or not.

So, from 1st statement: All plants are herbs, we get the figure: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b18f7937a34804b3ea34940a5f1146e870b9a7d998b1abe5d8d4bd7676ca605.png] 

Also, from 2nd statement: Some herbs are trees, we get the figure: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/faf22b7c7bc3f77da467aab6ea3dec9fac4d8e5ea7d75077db99f800ca30280b.png] 

And, from 3rd statement: All trees are shrubs, we get the figure:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c17f4b94aed59a3e906c9a4f229bd4d02b087a61eeb8b016b19e8bd0f2758231.png] 

Thus, combining all the three statements, we will get,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3bca329ec0295484050d807ddae8393bfc6a03b0c293bf8daf37ce9b9d7485a2.png] 

Next, we will check the conclusion from the given figure

I. Some shrubs are plants: This is not possible.

II. Some shrubs are herbs: This is true as we can see that some herbs are trees and all trees are shrubs. So this is true conclusion.

III. Some trees are plants: All plants are herbs and some herbs are trees. So, some trees cannot be plants and thus this is not true conclusion. 

Hence, only __**conclusion 2**__ is true.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term.

8 : 516 :: 6 : 219 :: 4 : ?
questions.solution:
Here, we need to find the pattern used to get the missing number.

As, we can see 8³ = 512 + 4 = 516

Next, 63 = 216 + 3 = 219

So, we can say the pattern followed here is that, they are taking the cube of the given number and then it is added by half of the given number.

Thus, for the given number 4, we will take cube of 4 i.e. 64 and then add half of 4 i.e. 2 to it to get the final answer as shown below:

4³ = 64 + 2 = 66

Hence, the final answer is __**66**__.
